blocks.text: סלוק.

מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ. עֶלְיוֹן עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ. יַכִּירוּ וְיֵדְעוּ כָּל הָאָרֶץ. כָּל יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל וְשֹׁכְנֵי אָרֶץ. מִקְצֵה הָאָרֶץ וְעַד קְצֵה הָאָרֶץ. כִּי הוּא בּוֹרֵא קְצוֹת כָּל הָאָרֶץ. עוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה בָּאָרֶץ. בְּקוּמוֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּט יַשְׁקִיט הָאָרֶץ. לְהוֹשִׁיעַ כָּל עַנְוֵי אָרֶץ. לַעֲשׂוֹת כַּתֹּהוּ שׁוֹפְטֵי הָאָרֶץ. לֶאֱחוֹז בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ. לְנַעֵר כָּל רִשְׁעֵי אָרֶץ. וְקוֹל יַשְׁמִיעוּ בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ. מָה אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ. וּבְמָלְכוֹ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ. יָרִיעוּ תַּחְתִּיּוֹת אָרֶץ. יִשְׂמְחוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְתָגֵל הָאָרֶץ. וַאֲשֶׁר בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל לָאָרֶץ. וַאֲשֶׁר בַּמַּיִם מִתַּחַת לָאָרֶץ. וְאָז יִפְצְחוּ רֶנֶן בָּאָרֶץ. כְּבוֹדוֹ מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ. יְיָ מָלָךְ תָּגֵל הָאָרֶץ. וּבְכֵן יְשַׁלֵּשׁ שׁוֹפְרוֹת עֶרֶץ. וְיַפְחִיד הוֹרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ. וְיַהֲפוֹךְ כִּסֵּא מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ. וְיֹאמְרוּ כָּל אֲשֶׁר נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ בָּאָרֶץ.
uncertainties: In several places a dagesh and the holam/shuruq choice are hard to see at this resolution, especially כַּתֹּהוּ, תַּחְתִּיּוֹת, יִפְצְחוּ and וְשֹׁכְנֵי.
Some instances of הָאָרֶץ / אָרֶץ may carry a meteg that I can't confirm.

blocks.text: 59 Morning Prayer for the New Year 59
Who forgives sins in judgment, Who is awe-inspiring in fame on the day of judgment,
Who pardons those carried by Him in judgment, Who answers those who call on Him on the day of judgment,
Who displays His compassion in judgment, Who observes what is concealed on the day of judgment,
Who acquires His slaves in judgment. Who has compassion on His people on the day of judgment,
uncertainties: The source has a period after 'in judgment' where the other rows have a comma. Transcribed as printed.

blocks.text: Who protects those who love Him, in judgment, Who supports His innocent ones on the day of judgment.
ובכן
And thus let sanctification arise for Thee, For Thou art our God, O King.
מלך

The King sustains the earth in justice. He is supreme over all the earth. The whole earth acknowledges and knows, all inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, from one end of the earth to the other, that He is Creator of the ends of all the earth who does justice and righteousness on earth. When for justice He rises in court — the earth is silent — to save all the humble of the earth, to make as nought the judges of the earth, to grasp the corners of the earth and throw off all the evil-doers of the earth. Then aloud do they proclaim in heaven and on earth: “How mighty is Thy Name throughout all the earth.” When He rules over all the earth, the depths of the earth shout with joy, the heavens rejoice and the earth exults together with what is in the heavens above the earth and what is in the waters below the earth. Then do they joyfully shout in adoration: “All the earth is full of His glory”. The Lord reigns, the earth rejoices. Three times will He let the Shofar blast be heard in dread and terrify the princes of dwellers on earth, and He will overthrow the thrones of the kingdoms of the earth so that all with breath in their nostrils on earth shall say: “How mighty is Thy Name throughout all the earth.” He establishes joy on the whole earth, arouses all who sleep in the earth, and they will lift up hymns of praise from the corner of the earth: “sing to the Lord, all the earth”.
uncertainties: The English has no counterparts to the Hebrew rubric סוגרים הארון. or the siglum ק׳; none was added.
The closing quotation marks are placed inconsistently ("glory”." and "earth”." against "earth.”"). Transcribed as printed.

notes: Biblical allusions in the Silluk, identified separately and not marked in the source: יעמיד ארץ (Prov 29:4); עליון על כל הארץ (Ps 83:19, 97:9); כל ישבי תבל ושכני ארץ (Isa 18:3); בורא קצות הארץ (Isa 40:28); עשה משפט וצדקה בארץ (Jer 9:23); בקומו למשפט... ארץ... שקטה... להושיע כל ענוי ארץ (Ps 76:9–10); לעשות כתהו שפטי ארץ (Isa 40:23); לאחז בכנפות הארץ וינערו רשעים (Job 38:13); מה אדיר שמך בכל הארץ (Ps 8:2, 8:10); הריעו תחתיות ארץ (Isa 44:23); ישמחו השמים ותגל הארץ (Ps 96:11); אשר בשמים ממעל... במים מתחת לארץ (Exod 20:4); פצחו רנה (Isa 49:13 etc.); מלא כל הארץ כבודו (Isa 6:3); ה׳ מלך תגל הארץ (Ps 97:1); כל אשר נשמת... באפיו (Gen 7:22); מכנף הארץ זמרת (Isa 24:16); שירו לה׳ כל הארץ (Ps 96:1). These are reviewer identifications; the source does not print citations.

Lael Orekh Din is read row by row: the right-column phrase (ending בַּדִּין) first, then the left-column phrase (ending בְּיוֹם דִּין) on the same line. On s147 the English is arranged the same way: left column (Hebrew right half), then right column.

The s146 page begins directly with the למוחל row. There is no ובכן דיין אמת אתה on this page, so nothing was skipped at the top. The tops of letters from the previous line are cut off at the top edge of band 1 and were ignored.
The band seams were resolved against the full page. Lines repeated across bands (the ארץ. ישמחו... line, the משוש... line, and the last English lines) are given once only.
Possible source issue, offered separately: in row 4 the English has a period ('in judgment.') where a comma is expected.
I took both page numbers from the printed headers: 59 on s146 and 59 on s147.
